Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC \u2014 a few clarifying Qs

1) For Dedicated capacity: can you confirm that customer data (inputs/outputs and KV/prefix cache) is logically separated per customer and not accessible to other tenants? Is the control plane shared?
2) For Private VPC/on-prem: does that include a private control plane option (no shared control plane) and support for our KMS (Azure Key Vault)?

Hi Alice \u2014 great questions, summarizing below so we\u2019re aligned and so I can loop in Dev for the technical details. Attaching our SOC2 summary and two short artifacts (Dedicated overview + Private VPC checklist).

Quick answers (TL;DR):
- Dedicated: dedicated GPU pools and per-customer runtime isolation. Customer model state (KV cache) and generated outputs are scoped to your tenant. The control plane is Redwood-managed (shared SaaS control plane) but we maintain strict tenancy at the data and runtime layers.
- Private VPC (VPC/on-prem): provides a private control plane option and VPC peering (or on-prem appliance) so networking and control-plane traffic do not traverse the shared Redwood control plane. You can bring your KMS (we support Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, and HSM integrations).
- Audit logs: both Dedicated and Private can provide detailed audit logs. With Dedicated you get tenant-scoped logs delivered to a secured storage endpoint (S3/GCS/Azure) with configurable retention. With Private we can additionally push logs into your internal SIEM over a private connection and support longer retention windows.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick technical sync (30m) with Dev to walk your compliance team through the differences and confirm KMS/retention requirements \u2014 can you share 2-3 time windows next week?
2) I\u2019ll send the SOC2 summary + Private VPC checklist (attached).
3) If you want, we can scope a short PoC on Dedicated first (no control-plane changes) to validate ingestion and encryption-at-rest, then evaluate Private VPC for full network isolation.

Attachments: Redwood-Dedicated-Overview.pdf, Redwood-Private-VPC-Checklist.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf

Thanks \u2014 happy to jump on whatever level of detail you need.

Best,

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC \u2014 a few clarifying Qs

Hi Alice \u2014 quick technical follow-up and clarifications from the infra side: 

- Dedicated:
  - Runtime/data isolation: compute (GPU) is reserved per customer pool; KV cache and model outputs are tenant-scoped. We do not co-mingle persistent storage across tenants.
  - Control plane: SaaS-managed (shared) control plane that handles orchestration, telemetry, and billing. Control-plane API calls are authenticated and scoped per customer.
  - Logs: we can stream audit logs to your storage account (S3/GCS/Azure) or to an HTTPS endpoint; retention is configurable (default 90 days, options up to multi-year on request).
  - KMS: We support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (Azure Key Vault supported).

- Private VPC / On-prem:
  - Private control plane option available for customers who require zero shared-control-plane exposure.
  - Supports VPC peering, PrivateLink, and on-prem appliance for air-gapped environments.
  - SIEM integration: direct log streaming into your internal SIEM over the private link.
  - Network controls: we can restrict egress to approved destinations and lock down public endpoints.

- PoC recommendation: Start with a non-prod Dedicated pool and have us deliver tenant-scoped logs and key-wrap with your Azure KV. That validates encryption, access controls, and logging. If you need full network segmentation, we can stand up a Private VPC in parallel for your security team to validate.

Happy to cover ports/IPs, retention SLAs, or KMS key rotation in the sync \u2014 propose Wed 4/14 or Thu 4/15 in the morning (PST).

\u2014Dev
